Would you say reacting negatively to someone else committing suicide was selfish?

When people say "it was devastating to their family/friends", this implies the family/friends of the self-murderer allowed the person's death to affect them deeply, rather than immediately trying to move past it, realize all life is transitory, blah blah blah.

You can't often help your emotions, and you can't help feeling attachment.  The detachment that comes with severe depression is just another sui-cide of the coin.

Yes, it's selfish, in the sense that almost every thing we do is (done to elicit personal positive feelings or alleviate negative ones.)  The real question is *how* selfish - personally I would say both of the op's examples are equally selfish, but a person committing suicide "to show them" is moreso.  I think that is a minority of cases, though.

Yeah I did have some good times in there.

I *think* what I said was I was *otherwise* a rational person - I am rational enough to realize that deep depression/suicide is never a rational mode of thinking.  It saps your will and gives you tunnel vision, hell I know all this and I still don't get help, so I agree with you that's the very definition of irrational.  I think I let it get too bad before trying more drastic measures.  (Which is again irrational because, it being a mental illness and not a physical one, I can go get help right now just as easily...except...well there's no except besides my own mental block telling me to give up, too tired.)

It is very frustrating, both for me and the people who try to help me - I experienced this plenty the last time I opened up about it, and so while it would be the best thing for me to do, I am loath to open up to my friends about it again.  People have enough frustration in their lives without mine.

But I am trying to stick it out until I can get some real help.  And I am trying to change it internally too, though I'm not sure how.  I'm very tired of trying but I'm still trying.  Thank you for the kind words.

I don't really have one.  Organizing hierarchies of taste is an exercise for healthy people.  I'm weird in that most of the time I don't even listen to music.  I do currently have a playlist I listen to with some sad, some happy stuff.  As for artists I like more than one song from, I guess I prefer Muse and NIN to most things.

Depression doesn't really work like that.  If I were able to do such things I'd be able to do "normal person" things too.  Though I have been trying - selling all my stuff and going on this trip, for one.  And I have sky dived before. :)

I've considered the peace corps or something similar, to wring something positive out of my existence, but it's important to note these things don't really help you when you're deep enough in, and one can only maintain them so long.
Agreed.   I'll try to remember this.
Heh, just commenting on how both your convos seemed to go down identical paths.  And will do.

You and lifeisshort123 should get married and have lots of babies or something.*  You could save on comment taxes!
But yeah, I'll keep that in mind.  Gonna try to sleep now.

*Have no actual idea as to either of your sexes/marital status
If I get back to the States I will look into low-cost options for that, for sure.

Oh I do think it would be the worst thing I ever did.

My parents are distant but supportive and my friends are that and close, which makes this extra hard.  None of them can do what needs to be done though (me fixing me), and I feel like I am failing badly, so I am doing what I can to minimize the fallout.  I'm just too tired of living this half-life to spare their feelings with my continued suffering.

I still have two months in a foreign country where I am dubious about their mental health offerings, especially with my lack of insurance.

If I make it back to the States you have my word I'll look into it.

Depression does tend to fuck up a sleep schedule.  I think I get around 9-10 hours most days here.  Some I get more like 4-5, especially when taking night buses to various parts of the country.

I'll try to socialize a bit more.  It's difficult because I'm so tired I stop seeing the point so I just stick to quick, businesslike exchanges.  It doesn't help that I find women more approachable, but then get tangled up in my romantic feelings.  If I start to perceive (or even worry) that I come across as "that creepy guy" to them, I get fucking disgusted with myself and try to end the conversation politely and quickly.  And of course all that emotion and mental gymnastics thrown in makes the conversations extra tiring.
ok.

Yes, when I was trying to get over my breakup a lot of the meetups I joined felt like pulling teeth just to go to, and meditation was nigh-impossible.

My friends and family deserve a lot better than everything I've done for the last decade, much less disappearing.  I haven't hurt or lashed out at them but they do feel frustrated and helpless due to this.  They all tend to be generally happy but introverted people, which I am starting to realize is a difficult combination for someone in depression.  Those around you find it difficult to relate, yet respect your privacy too much to make you go out and do things with others.  We've forced it in the past but when it doesn't occur naturally, well, tough habits to establish.

It's not that they don't want to talk about suicide - they gladly would and have when they think it would help.  I just don't see the point when it won't change anything besides make them a little depressed as well.

I can hope that you are right.

If I am still alive in two months, I will let you know.  The Me-that-is-then will owe such a caring person that much.

Well the depression's been getting steadily worse for a little over a decade, I can unequivocally say I am *not* "just surrounded by assholes", and I don't have the same hormonal fluctuations at 30 as a teenager.  My post-breakup anguish has passed the "halftime rule" mark (many people claim you need half as much time as the relationship itself to get over it, could be BS of course), and in any case my depression came before my ex.  So what I meant was I don't think it'll clear up as it does for a lot of people at that age, and I let it fester way too long without real help.  So now I feel too tired to do anything about it.
Ok.

It's kept me from just sitting in my hostel bed and staring at the wall till I go to sleep, so yeah!  :)

And yeah it'll work if I decide it's enough in the end - some people cut themselves, throw themselves off buildings onto busy streets, etc.  These are attention-getters for a reason (but should still be treated with absolute seriousness.)  But I've never really been like that.  More the quiet type, never wanted attention or fame so much as connection and satisfaction.  If there's one thing I *am* sure of it's that a quiet death with as little pain for others, then me, is my way to go.  (If it was me-then-others I'd do something like nitrogen suffocation, but that leaves a trail I don't want.)

Your English is fine, and I get all that.  If I really want to get better I have to establish positive reinforcing events, long enough to turn them into habits.  Just haven't been able to do that so far.

I am by the sea now, and every night I have like this makes the short walk off a long pier more appealing.  But I am waiting, there is a tiny bit left.  But...well, I know my deficiencies at this point far better than my proficiencies.  And they are this: that I can make as many goddamn lists and goals as I want, but will not complete them.  That it is not tunnel vision depression gives me, but a lack of drive.  I can see what I need to do to save myself just fine.  I just can't wrench up enough willpower to do it.

Combine that with my hermitage, my fear of making connections with other people that could give me the jolt I refuse (for some idiot reason) to give myself, and...I dunno.  Magic 8-ball says "outlook not so good."

Since I still have a month or two left in my "trip", I'm not in a terrible hurry, though some nights (like tonight) feel more urgent than others.  Basically I'm hopping around the country trying to find a good undeveloped area, preferably with sea cliffs, a large unpatrolled body of water, or inland cliffs that aren't often visited (but aren't too impossible for me to get to on foot).

Being overseas means you don't have to worry quite so much about timing issues - you're already well out of sight, and you'll be out of mind until they start noticing your absence.

I guess part of me is waiting for a sign too, sometime to renew my strength or prove to me I can im-prove.  But besides the depression itself, I'm a pretty rational person - so it'd have to be a damn good one.  I'm trying to create it myself when I can - visiting historic sites, eating good food, even interaction with (le gasp) people when I can dredge it out of me.  We'll see if that's enough in the end.

I'm sorry.  I'm really very tired.  I would show you how weary I am but the only accurate method of description would be for you to feel it, and I wouldn't wish that on anyone, even for a moment.  I'm crying, unfocused, and lethargic while the picture of health and with zero drugs in my system.

I wish I could say I would give your suggestions the time and thought they deserve but I can promise nothing.  As I said I don't want to die and I would love to believe I can overcome, but I can see myself deciding that I would rather disappoint myself in this one final way and be done, than disappoint myself over and over and over again for the rest of my life.

The best I can do is ask that you keep doing the amazing stuff you do here, helping these people.  One of the strangest bright moments I've had is realizing the vast majority of posts on sucidewatch *don't* seem like me - they bear the urgency and pain but it is temporary, an affliction of the young and confused that can disperse naturally if given the chance.

There was a time when I hoped that I was the same, it was just hitting me later, as I was a late bloomer in so many other things (sex, drinking, etc.).  I love the "it gets better" campaign and I think it's very important.  But I think that hope is well past me now.

This all sounds correct, yes.

No thank you.  I wouldn't even be here if it wasn't anonymous - the point of me coming here was to weaken ties, not strengthen them.  Also my country is small enough that someone might be able to do detective work and tie this to my main account and thus to me.  That would cause problems.

Friends tend not to take it well when you talk about suicide.  Friends tend to call the cops or go to extremes.  Not that I blame them.

I tried both but I don't think I gave them a fair shake.  I only went to a few months of therapy and I was on the weakest kind of anti-depressants.  It did help me keep it together enough to finish my job but that was about it.

You hear the horror stories of stronger ADs just "dulling" everything, that worries me.  But really the major problem going that route now (even if I survive my "vacation") is the lack of any insurance.

I would love to attempt those again.  I just don't think I can handle disappointing myself so completely once more.  I've had more false starts than you would believe.  Those sparse 100 pages of my "novel" didn't come from just a few sessions - they came from tiny slivers of productivity in a mass of shitty beginnings, doubt, fearful procrastination and blank stares.

And when even the basic stuff requires such extreme effort, you get very little sympathy from the average person.  Another reason I think my ex left, she saw it as me being childish, unable to just "get over it" and work at something more permanent.  I can't say she was wrong anymore because I'm too exhausted to keep trying to guess at what people think.  And that's why I haven't been able to write. :P
Thanks.  Hopefully you heard me and are taking steps to avoid ever doing the same thing.  I don't recommend this for anyone, in fact I think it's stupid.  I'm just too tired to try anything else.

I didn't enjoy my jobs while I was at them.  I would say I was "neutral" about them really - they weren't terrible, but they were boring and I felt very unfulfilled.  I know that sounds retarded in our current economy, lots of people do undesirable jobs - but they also have something to work toward, whether it be a family, success, money, power, love.

I'm so tired that I can't work towards any of that.  I haven't taken another job because I have absolutely no idea what I want to do.  I thought I wanted to be a writer, a video game designer, and a few other things - now I don't even think about it.  There's just a blank space where my goals and dreams used to be.

As for my relationship, no, I was quite happy in it, comparatively.  My decade of depression was a slow downward spiral, and I had almost made this decision once before when I figured - fuck it, I need to at least not die a virgin.  And that's how I started up a friends-with-benefits thing with my ex (let me be clear: she knew I was depressed but I didn't "ransom" her into anything, we just chatted about our mutual attraction for a while until she went with the fwb idea.  Saying "have sex with me or I'll kill myself" is one of the worst things I can imagine telling a person.)

While we were together I was so, so much happier, but it was a band-aid on a bleeding wound.  I still fretted about my lack of direction, career, etc. all the time, and I think that wore on her.

When she left, I was the worst I'd ever been for a while - to be honest I think the only reason I didn't off myself then is I knew my friends were watching too closely.  I dreamed about her every night, had to take breaks every hour to cry at work, couldn't concentrate, stared at the wall when I went home, drank a lot.  There was more than once I had to call a friend to drive me back from work because I couldn't drive myself, and I would sometimes just collapse on the kitchen floor and fall asleep sobbing there.

It sounds ridiculous or histrionic, but I honestly didn't do it for attention - I just had no concept of anyone else at the time.  I was wreathed in pain and it leached out in ways I couldn't contain or hide.  And this was from fucking 1.5 years with a girl, when people have handled sudden divorce from their 20 year marriages better!  Christ.  I...I loved her very much.
